blockers: The signature gesture strip is not a legible signature gesture: the 24 frames read almost entirely as minor idle variations, with no clear anticipation, action pose, overshoot, or settled impact.
Facial construction is effectively a bald spherical head with a tiny isolated eye/white facial patch. At native scale it reads as unfinished and mildly uncanny rather than a designed face.

The character's heavy physical identity is not convincingly animated. Locomotion moves the limbs, but the torso remains too rigid and upright; there is insufficient compression, counter-rotation, or mass transfer for a broad impact-oriented fighter.

Material rendering is overly smooth and airbrushed for the intended retro-anachronistic readability. The torso, skin, bronze, and vambraces rely on similar soft highlight bands, causing them to read as inflated plastic forms instead of distinct materials.

The front silhouette has a large dead black gap between the legs and weak separation around the hanging arms and equipment. The broad torso dominates so heavily that the lower-body rhythm becomes two generic vertical columns.

Several locomotion directions collapse toward the same front-facing broad-body pose. The 8-direction set has directional coverage, but not enough distinct silhouette rhythm or torso orientation to make the views feel authored rather than interpolated.
high_value_changes: Redesign the signature gesture as a readable heavy-action cycle: crouched anticipation, clear shield or weapon drive, one-frame overshoot with asymmetric torso compression, then a visible weighted settle. Keep the ground anchor fixed while allowing hips, shoulders, and head to recoil.

Replace the spherical blank head with a compact, readable facial design: establish a brow or hairline, eye placement, nose or cheek break, and a controlled shadow shape that survives at 1x without becoming noise.
Push Agnes's body mechanics toward a lower center of gravity. Add hip drop, planted support-leg compression, shoulder counter-tilt, and delayed head/pauldron follow-through during steps and impacts.

Rebuild the palette by separating value roles: darker rust or brown torso shadow, clearly distinct ochre armor, restrained bronze speculars, and separated skin values. Reduce broad gradients and use deliberate clustered highlights.
Open and shape the lower-body silhouette. Vary leg spacing, knee bends, boot angles, and support-leg width so the stance communicates mass instead of producing two parallel bars.

Author the oblique and rear directions independently enough to preserve the asymmetric pauldron, buckler, and weapon hierarchy. Each direction should expose a different silhouette and weight distribution.
optional_notes: The measured 122.8px standing height and zero anchor drift satisfy the technical contract; these are not the cause of failure.

Against the supplied Celina comparison, Agnes is materially and proportionally distinct: Agnes is broader, warmer, and more horizontally massed, while Celina is narrow and vertically elongated. There is no severe body-type convergence in this comparison.

The warm ochre, rust, bronze, and flesh combination is directionally appropriate, but the current highlight treatment makes the palette feel closer to generic glossy armor than deliberately earthy SaGa styling.
The 4x nearest-neighbor sheet is useful for inspection, but the native 1x read remains the decisive test; small facial and equipment details currently disappear or merge there.
regressions_from_previous: No direct round-01 Agnes sheets or animation exports were provided, so frame-level regressions from the previous round cannot be verified.

Relative to the previously accepted Celina roster reference, Agnes does not show a major silhouette or body-type convergence; the more serious issue is insufficient internal distinction between Agnes's own action, idle, and directional poses.
strongest_improvements: The broad torso, asymmetric shoulder mass, left-side equipment cluster, and planted boots establish a potentially useful heavy-fighter silhouette.
The technical placement is disciplined: standing height remains below the limit and the ground anchor does not jitter.
The warm palette separates Agnes from the supplied blue, narrow Celina reference at a roster level.
luna_evaluation.single_most_important_next_change: Replace the current signature gesture strip with a genuinely readable heavy-impact action cycle, built around crouch anticipation, asymmetric drive, torso recoil, and a weighted settle while preserving the fixed ground anchor.
